Resolves to the party that wins the November 7, 2028 U.S. House election in Alabama's 4th District: whichever district is numbered 4 on the map in effect for that election. N/A if that map has no district numbered 4.

Only the party matters: a Democratic or Republican nominee counts as that party even if also listed on other parties' lines. Anyone else resolves to Other, or to their own answer if one has been added.

Resolves on the certified result, or earlier once the AP has called the race and no recount could change it. N/A if no election for this seat is held.

seed.basis: Opening odds are a starting point, not a forecast. Alabama's 4th District voted 65.4 points more Republican than the country in the 2024 presidential election (on its current lines); pulled toward even for a race this far off, that gives Democrats 1% and Republicans 98%. Other opens at 1%.
seed.note: Initial pool probabilities only. Not an observed market forecast. Stage A prior (SEEDS.md).

resultsSource.downballot: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eZfaFI-c-PFOoKx1-zZA2MP0_dxRq_LVK0re3BOQqy0 (exact totals tab, 2024 results on 2026 district lines; 2020 only where lines are unchanged), via https://www.the-downballot.com/p/the-downballots-calculations-of-presidential

liquidityPlan.rationale: Default tier 1,000: a generic market opened years ahead. Raise it as the cycle approaches if the race becomes competitive enough that a Ṁ100 trade should move the price by a point rather than ten.
liquidityPlan.alternatives: Lower: tier 100 (not recommended; repeats the shallow-market problem). Higher: tier 10,000 (the rule for 2028 presidential and competitive races) or +extraLiquidity.

evidence.seat: 4th district on the map in effect for the 2026 election; term beginning January 3, 2029

redistricting.mapInUse2026: Legislature's June 2, 2026 map, after the Supreme Court lifted the Allen v. Milligan injunction (June 2, 2026) in the wake of Callais
redistricting.note: Lines changed for 2026 (2020 presidential results are not available on these lines). Litigation against the new map remains possible.

entries.shapeRationale: Generic ballot-party multi (Democratic Party / Republican Party, plus the server's "Other"), opened years ahead with no candidates named. Party outcomes survive nominee changes and map directly to seat and elector totals; answers sum to one, and only @ManifoldPolitics can add an answer (a third party or a named independent), which takes its share out of "Other".

Resolves to the party that wins the November 7, 2028 U.S. House election in Georgia's 2nd District: whichever district is numbered 2 on the map in effect for that election. N/A if that map has no district numbered 2. If no candidate gets a majority, the December 5, 2028 runoff decides.

Only the party matters: a Democratic or Republican nominee counts as that party even if also listed on other parties' lines. Anyone else resolves to Other, or to their own answer if one has been added.

Resolves on the certified result, or earlier once the AP has called the race and no recount could change it. N/A if no election for this seat is held.

seed.basis: Opening odds are a starting point, not a forecast. Georgia's 2nd District voted 7.5 points more Democratic than the country in the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections; pulled toward even for a race this far off, that gives Democrats 76.6% and Republicans 22.4%. Other opens at 1%.
seed.note: Initial pool probabilities only. Not an observed market forecast. Stage A prior (SEEDS.md).

resultsSource.downballot: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eZfaFI-c-PFOoKx1-zZA2MP0_dxRq_LVK0re3BOQqy0 (exact totals tab, 2024 results on 2026 district lines; 2020 only where lines are unchanged), via https://www.the-downballot.com/p/the-downballots-calculations-of-presidential

liquidityPlan.rationale: Default tier 1,000: a generic market opened years ahead. Raise it as the cycle approaches if the race becomes competitive enough that a Ṁ100 trade should move the price by a point rather than ten.
liquidityPlan.alternatives: Lower: tier 100 (not recommended; repeats the shallow-market problem). Higher: tier 10,000 (the rule for 2028 presidential and competitive races) or +extraLiquidity.

evidence.seat: 2nd district on the map in effect for the 2026 election; term beginning January 3, 2029

redistricting.note: Gov. Kemp's June 17, 2026 special session was called to redraw for 2028 after Callais; legislators declined to take up maps. A redraw in the 2027 regular session remains likely to be attempted. Senate and House generals have a majority/runoff rule (runoff December 5, 2028).

identity.round: the November 7, 2028 general election if a candidate wins a majority of the votes; otherwise the December 5, 2028 runoff between the top two (O.C.G.A. § 21-2-501: majority required, runoff on the 28th day after)

entries.shapeRationale: Generic ballot-party multi (Democratic Party / Republican Party, plus the server's "Other"), opened years ahead with no candidates named. Party outcomes survive nominee changes and map directly to seat and elector totals; answers sum to one, and only @ManifoldPolitics can add an answer (a third party or a named independent), which takes its share out of "Other".

Resolves to the party that wins the November 7, 2028 U.S. House election in Nevada's 3rd District: whichever district is numbered 3 on the map in effect for that election. N/A if that map has no district numbered 3.

Only the party matters: a Democratic or Republican nominee counts as that party even if also listed on other parties' lines. Anyone else resolves to Other, or to their own answer if one has been added.

Resolves on the certified result, or earlier once the AP has called the race and no recount could change it. N/A if no election for this seat is held.

seed.basis: Opening odds are a starting point, not a forecast. Nevada's 3rd District voted 1.5 points more Democratic than the country in the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections; pulled toward even for a race this far off, that gives Democrats 55.4% and Republicans 43.6%. Other opens at 1%.
seed.note: Initial pool probabilities only. Not an observed market forecast. Stage A prior (SEEDS.md).

resultsSource.downballot: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eZfaFI-c-PFOoKx1-zZA2MP0_dxRq_LVK0re3BOQqy0 (exact totals tab, 2024 results on 2026 district lines; 2020 only where lines are unchanged), via https://www.the-downballot.com/p/the-downballots-calculations-of-presidential

liquidityPlan.rationale: Competitive: within 5 points of the national environment (2028 House district): Ṁ10,000.

evidence.seat: 3rd district on the map in effect for the 2026 election; term beginning January 3, 2029

entries.shapeRationale: Generic ballot-party multi (Democratic Party / Republican Party, plus the server's "Other"), opened years ahead with no candidates named. Party outcomes survive nominee changes and map directly to seat and elector totals; answers sum to one, and only @ManifoldPolitics can add an answer (a third party or a named independent), which takes its share out of "Other".

Resolves to the party that wins the November 7, 2028 U.S. House election in Ohio's 11th District: whichever district is numbered 11 on the map in effect for that election. N/A if that map has no district numbered 11.

Only the party matters: a Democratic or Republican nominee counts as that party even if also listed on other parties' lines. Anyone else resolves to Other, or to their own answer if one has been added.

Resolves on the certified result, or earlier once the AP has called the race and no recount could change it. N/A if no election for this seat is held.

seed.basis: Opening odds are a starting point, not a forecast. Ohio's 11th District voted 57.0 points more Democratic than the country in the 2024 presidential election (on its current lines); pulled toward even for a race this far off, that gives Democrats 98% and Republicans 1%. Other opens at 1%.
seed.note: Initial pool probabilities only. Not an observed market forecast. Stage A prior (SEEDS.md).

resultsSource.downballot: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eZfaFI-c-PFOoKx1-zZA2MP0_dxRq_LVK0re3BOQqy0 (exact totals tab, 2024 results on 2026 district lines; 2020 only where lines are unchanged), via https://www.the-downballot.com/p/the-downballots-calculations-of-presidential

liquidityPlan.rationale: Default tier 1,000: a generic market opened years ahead. Raise it as the cycle approaches if the race becomes competitive enough that a Ṁ100 trade should move the price by a point rather than ten.
liquidityPlan.alternatives: Lower: tier 100 (not recommended; repeats the shallow-market problem). Higher: tier 10,000 (the rule for 2028 presidential and competitive races) or +extraLiquidity.

evidence.seat: 11th district on the map in effect for the 2026 election; term beginning January 3, 2029

redistricting.mapInUse2026: October 31, 2025 commission map (unanimous), in force through 2031
redistricting.note: 2020 results are not available on these lines.

entries.shapeRationale: Generic ballot-party multi (Democratic Party / Republican Party, plus the server's "Other"), opened years ahead with no candidates named. Party outcomes survive nominee changes and map directly to seat and elector totals; answers sum to one, and only @ManifoldPolitics can add an answer (a third party or a named independent), which takes its share out of "Other".

Resolves to the party that wins the November 7, 2028 U.S. House election in Texas's 27th District: whichever district is numbered 27 on the map in effect for that election. N/A if that map has no district numbered 27.

Only the party matters: a Democratic or Republican nominee counts as that party even if also listed on other parties' lines. Anyone else resolves to Other, or to their own answer if one has been added.

Resolves on the certified result, or earlier once the AP has called the race and no recount could change it. N/A if no election for this seat is held.

seed.basis: Opening odds are a starting point, not a forecast. Texas's 27th District voted 20.0 points more Republican than the country in the 2024 presidential election (on its current lines); pulled toward even for a race this far off, that gives Democrats 2.3% and Republicans 96.7%. Other opens at 1%.
seed.note: Initial pool probabilities only. Not an observed market forecast. Stage A prior (SEEDS.md).

resultsSource.downballot: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eZfaFI-c-PFOoKx1-zZA2MP0_dxRq_LVK0re3BOQqy0 (exact totals tab, 2024 results on 2026 district lines; 2020 only where lines are unchanged), via https://www.the-downballot.com/p/the-downballots-calculations-of-presidential

liquidityPlan.rationale: Default tier 1,000: a generic market opened years ahead. Raise it as the cycle approaches if the race becomes competitive enough that a Ṁ100 trade should move the price by a point rather than ten.
liquidityPlan.alternatives: Lower: tier 100 (not recommended; repeats the shallow-market problem). Higher: tier 10,000 (the rule for 2028 presidential and competitive races) or +extraLiquidity.

evidence.seat: 27th district on the map in effect for the 2026 election; term beginning January 3, 2029

redistricting.note: The Supreme Court stayed the November 2025 injunction (December 4, 2025) and reversed the district court in April 2026 (Abbott v. LULAC); merits litigation continues. 2020 results are not available on these lines.

entries.shapeRationale: Generic ballot-party multi (Democratic Party / Republican Party, plus the server's "Other"), opened years ahead with no candidates named. Party outcomes survive nominee changes and map directly to seat and elector totals; answers sum to one, and only @ManifoldPolitics can add an answer (a third party or a named independent), which takes its share out of "Other".
